chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Suqah, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The people are not healed with the likes of (healing with) the honey.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq)
key_terms.اسْتَشْفَى: To seek healing / to be healed

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of honey in Shia Islamic tradition regarding health and healing?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) declares honey as the most effective remedy for healing, reflecting the Shia emphasis on practical medicine (*al-tibb*) as a means of preserving health. This statement underscores the prophetic tradition of utilizing natural substances for therapeutic purposes, a practice deeply rooted in both Islamic teachings and the medical knowledge of the time. The narration highlights honey's unique status not just as food, but as a superior medicinal agent recognized by the Imams.
